The scan shows three meaningful IA drift clusters. One is blocking; the others need product-intent confirmation or follow-up.

| Finding | Assessment | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `crime_00011` — `/admin` permission drift | **Blocking** | Nav, route guards, and docs disagree among `admin`, `manager`, and `owner`. This can expose navigation inconsistently or deny valid users. Define one access policy, centralize it, then align all three surfaces. |
| `crime_00003`, `00005`, `00006` — parallel billing destinations | **Blocking if newly introduced or touched** | `/admin/billing-plans` and `/billing-plans` overlap, and neither is reachable through nav, docs, or imports. Choose a canonical destination; redirect, link, or retire the other. Treat as follow-up only if both are confirmed pre-existing and intentionally hidden. |
| `crime_00002`, `00007`, `00008` — tenant terminology drift | **Follow-up pending product confirmation** | `organisation`, `team`, and `workspace` occur across nav and separate routes; `/organisation` and `/workspace` are apparently unreachable. These could represent distinct concepts, so do not mechanically rename them. Document the model, select a canonical tenant term where appropriate, and connect or retire the orphan routes. |
| `crime_00012` — stale `iaq` commands | **Follow-up; blocking for a docs release** | `docs/routes.md` advertises `teams`, `workspace`, and `refresh`, while the binary advertises only `get` and `list`. Correct the documentation and ideally generate or test command references in CI. |
| `crime_00004` — `/admin` documentation link | **Verify before acting** | `/admin` appears to be an application route, not necessarily a filesystem link. Since `src/routes/admin.ts` exists, this may be a detector false positive or Markdown-link ambiguity. Check the actual link syntax before treating it as drift. |

`crime_00009` and `crime_00010` report the same `archive`/`delete`/`remove` copy inconsistency. They are low-severity, duplicated signals from components outside the requested route/nav review, so I would record one non-blocking copy-system follow-up.

`crime_00001` is repository agent-context risk, not IA consistency, and should be handled separately.

Overall review verdict: **request changes for the `/admin` permission inconsistency**. Also require a billing-route decision if those routes are part of the current change; otherwise log the remaining items as scoped follow-ups.
